definition: SOURCE PACKET ONLY. Gestational rules and exceptions require a compound contract. No scalar admission or historical enforceability is established.
summarySource: T6 inventory 2a2ed6cc6e247fe616a7574e84b4799e32ada60a and captured public sources in retrieval-index.json. Inherited summaries are labeled below. Source Table 2 footnotes: Notes: Table includes only those jurisdictions with policies relevant to this topic in effect. The inclusion of an exception in a policy banning abortion does not ensure there will be a provider available or willing to perform the procedure. The exceptions listed are for abortion bans that are in effect. Gestational duration limits that differ from the overall limit are noted and are in LMP unless otherwise stated. *On August 13, 2026, the United States District Court for the District of Idaho expanded Idaho’s exceptions to include threats to the physical health and general health of the pregnant person. However, a court later narrowed this ruling only to care provided by the physician plaintiff, meaning that only one provider is permitted to provide care under the expanded exceptions. †Maine allows for abortion after viability when a physician deems it necessary. In Illinois, the health of the patient encompasses “all factors that are relevant to the patient’s health and well-being, including, but not limited to, physical, emotional, psychological, and familial health and age.” In both states, the broad nature of the exceptions allows care to be provided later in pregnancy. ‡In Iowa, the rape and incest exceptions require sexual assault survivors to report the incident to law enforcement or a health agency within 45 days and survivors of incest to report the assault within 140 days.

US-NH.note: Reviewed current RSA 329:44: prohibits at least 24 weeks probable gestational age except fetal abnormalities incompatible with life or defined medical emergency. Emergency covers endangered life from physical disorder, illness or injury, including pregnancy conditions, or serious risk of substantial and irreversible impairment of a major bodily function. Current page lists January 1, 2022 and May 2022 amendments. SOURCE PACKET ONLY: no scalar admission or historical-date assertion. Artifact abortion-source-21. Table 2 source cells: Threat to the life of the pregnant person = X; Threat to the physical health of the pregnant person = X; Diagnosis of lethal fetal anomaly = X. Artifact abortion-source-22. Source footnotes and measurement definitions are preserved in raw/abortion-source-22.txt; X denotes the source table marking, not an executable legal predicate. This later snapshot does not establish January 1, 2026 or fallback-2000 enforceability. ADDITIONAL PRIMARY AUTHORITY: captured RSA 329:43 (artifact nh-definitions) defines gestational age as elapsed time since the first day of the last menstrual period; probable gestational age and reasonable medical judgment are separate defined terms. Major bodily function includes immune, cell growth, digestive, bowel, bladder, neurological, brain, respiratory, circulatory, endocrine and reproductive functions. Abortion definition excludes removal of ectopic pregnancy, dead fetus from spontaneous abortion, and acts intended to save fetal life or health. Both definitions and prohibition source histories identify 2021 chapter 91 section 39 effective January 1, 2022. The prohibition additionally lists 2022 chapter 86 section 1 effective May 20, 2022 and chapter 119 section 1 effective May 27, 2022. These are sourced statutory dates, not proof of court enforceability or the full January 1, 2026 historical version. The inventory fallback January 1, 2000 is contradicted as the start of this cited subdivision. No schema, scalar or live-law date is admitted.
